citations.narrative:
* Approximately 25% of the floor was covered with bedding, feathers, vermin waste, brown dust, webs, hair and pieces of
white Styrofoam insulation. The pieces of insulation and vermin waste indicate an ongoing vermin infestation. The ceiling
and the white plastic legs for the sink had black to reddish brown grimy spots covering approximately 30% of their
surfaces. The metal lids on the trash cans, plastic storage containers and shelves had an accumulation of brown dust,
brown grime, white pieces of insulation and vermin waste on top of their lids. This indicates there are not enough
provisions to remove or dispose of animal and food waste, bedding, grime and insect waste on hard surfaces and the
debris. As a result, there is a vermin infestation, and numerous insects flying around in the building. This can increase the
potential for other disease hazards for the 31 Guinea Pigs.
For the prevention and accumulation of animal and food waste, bedding, black to brown grimy spots on the hard surfaces,
debris, and to minimize vermin, insects and disease hazards for all guinea pigs, additional provisions of removal and
disposal must be implemented.

* Eight watering receptacles used to water 10 guinea pigs had an accumulation of brown debris and or dirt and vermin
fecal waste on top plastic surface of the receptacles. These receptacles indicate that they are not being sanitized when
dirty or at least every two weeks. When asked how often the water receptacles were cleaned, the licensee stated they
don’t have a schedule for cleaning. As a result, this can increase the disease potential for the animals.
For the prevention of the disease potential, all water receptacles must be sanitized when dirty and or at least once every
two weeks.
To be corrected by, 3-July-2026

* Eight enclosures, housing 16 guinea pigs, have an accumulation of reddish specks of grime on the white cage surfaces.
This indicates the enclosures are not being cleaned to prevent an accumulation of debris, and sanitization at least once
every two weeks does not happen. Therefore, this can increase the disease hazards for the guinea pigs.
For the prevention of disease hazards to the guinea pigs, all enclosures must be cleaned and sanitized often enough for
the prevention of an accumulation of excreta and debris.
To be corrected by, 6-July-2026.

* There was a live mouse that ran across the floor under a raised rabbit enclosure during the inspection and quickly
scampered into hiding. The licensee stated that the mice were coming in through the floor, and that they had repaired the
building with mouse prevention under part of the building. Similarly, the licensee stated, they used different traps to trap
the mice. There were not any traps present during the inspection. There were mouse droppings on the table where the
clean feeding bowls were stored. The mouse fecal waste droppings were on the floor around the sink area and husbandry
work area and on top of lids for plastic storage containers and water bottles used as watering receptacles. Numerous
pieces of Styrofoam insulation from inside the wall were on the floor around the sink area from the mice getting into the
building. Numerous small insects (small flies) were observed flying around the ceiling by a hanging light. Similarly, small
flies were flying above the melon rind inside the turtle enclosure. The licensee had a homemade bottle trap near the turtle
enclosure. However, there was only one bottle trap for prevention of the insects.
The presence of mice and small flies indicates that there is not an established and maintained program to control insects
and mammalian pests. As a result, this can increase the disease hazards for the 31 guinea pigs.
For the prevention of disease hazards for all guinea pigs, an effective program to control insects and mammalian pests
must be established and maintained.
